text:
maya: Noticing a recurring latency oscillation on multi-GPU runs after the CUDA-graph capture change we shipped yesterday. Allreduce tail latency jumps every ~30s and throughput dips by ~12% :thinking:

liam: Yikes. Is this the same batch mix as before? sequence lengths or kv-cache warmup patterns changed?

maya: Batch mix is identical. The only diff was enabling graph_pooling and pin_graph_streams=true in the runtime.

andre: Can you paste a short perf trace? nvprof / nsight timeline snapshot would help.

maya: Quick flame from nsight for a spike window:
```
GPU0: compute(stream2) [0.2ms] -> memcpyH2D -> compute(stream0) blocks -> ncclAllReduce(stream1) [5.6ms]
GPU1: compute(stream2) [0.21ms] -> ncclAllReduce(stream1) [8.3ms] -> compute(stream0)
// Noticeable reordering: allreduce ends later on GPU1
```

caro: That ordering smells like streams getting phase-shifted across devices under graph replay. If capture pins different stream IDs per epoch, NCCL may launch at different times and allreduce sees imbalance.

liam: I ran a microbench: fixed-graph vs replayed-graph on 8xA100. With replayed-graph we get periodic 10-15% allreduce latency jitter. With capture disabled it's stable.

andre: Does kernel selector change kernel variant under certain seq len windows? If graph capture serializes a particular kernel path, but the selector later switches quantized kernels, the launch shapes could differ and disrupt overlap.

maya: Good call. I profiled kernel names. We saw fluctuating picks between fast_fp16_kern_v3 and fallback_fp16_compat. When fallback picks happen it takes slightly longer on rank1, creating slip. Not purely NCCL issue.

ci-bot: deploy-notify: reverted graph_pooling to previous flag in canary at 1715004000 per rollback policy.

liam: Thanks. Can we reproduce locally? I have a repro script that runs 200 epochs with synthetic seq length distribution (5/25/1024 mixture).

maya: Repro script:```bash
python bench/mpi_repro.py --gpus 8 --epochs 200 --seq-dist "0.6:5,0.3:25,0.1:1024" --use-cuda-graph --pin-graph-streams
```
Produces the oscillation within ~40 epochs.

caro: Two hypotheses: (1) capture assigns stream ids non-deterministically across GPUs leading to NCCL schedule skew, (2) kernel selector is stateful and adapts mid-run causing compute skew that amplifies allreduce queuing.

andre: For (1) we can force stream affinity: setStreamPriority(stream0, high) and a fixed stream index at capture time as a test. For (2) we'd make kernel selector stateless per model config and log every kernel choice.

liam: I added verbose kernel-select logs and saw that on the spike epochs the selector switched due to an observed micro-batch sequence length change triggered by our KV prefetcher fallback (it thought cache misses spiked).

maya: So KV cache warmup -> different micro-batch shapes -> selector picks fallback kernel -> per-device compute skew -> NCCL waits longer on slow rank -> tail latency spike. All connected.

caro: Nice root cause chain. Two mitigations: (A) make kernel selector robust to transient seq-length blips (prefer sticky selection for N steps), (B) make capture stream mapping deterministic and add a tiny inter-stream fence before collective launches when using graphs.

andre: Also add a simple smoothing to KV prefetcher to avoid sudden fallback on a single miss (exponential backoff or require two consecutive misses).

liam: I prototyped sticky selector (stick 8 iterations) and re-ran. Oscillation disappears in the run I did, throughput stable.

maya: Great. Can we ship sticky selector behind a flag and add telemetry to monitor kernel churn?

ci-bot: perf-alert: created ticket PERF-1942 with logs and repro link.

caro: I'll own making capture mapping deterministic and adding the inter-stream fence option. andre, can you own the sticky selector toggle and telemetry?

andre: Yep. I'll also add a short opt-in test in CI that runs the repro for 50 epochs on 4 GPUs to catch regressions.

maya: Thanks all. Rolling the canary back fixed production but we should get the two fixes in next patch. Leaving logs and nsight traces at s3://redwood-perf/1715002468/ for anyone who wants them. :thumbsup:

liam: Patch plan: sticky-selector flag (runtime.cfg: kernel_selector.sticky_iters=8), kv.prefetch.smoothing=true, capture.stream_deterministic=true. I'll open PRs.

maya: Closing the loop here once PRs link. Won't forget to add a note in release notes about graph/sticky interactions.

caro: Also add regression test to ensure allreduce tail latency < 12ms for our standard multi-gpu smoke.

ci-bot: ticket PERF-1942 assigned to caro, andre, liam. Due: 1715600000.
